text: [serious, cinematic storyteller, brisk pace] The fire started at midnight. By sunrise, city hall was gone. Three days earlier, it was only a whisper. The mayor had sold the city's water. There was no proof. There didn't need to be. By the second day, a million people filled the streets. Banners hung from every bridge. Half the city wanted him gone. The other half swore he was innocent. On the third night, someone threw the first flame. The mayor vanished. No one knows if he ran… or if he was taken. For two days, the city had no one. No water. No bread. No answers. Then, on the fifth day, a man walked out of the ashes. No name. No past. He handed out bread. He spoke softly. Everything he said sounded true. By the seventh day, the stadium was full. And he told them God had sent him. Half the city fell to its knees. The Prophet warned that before the Hour, around thirty liars would come, each claiming to be a messenger of God. The next morning, the neighboring city heard his name.
